newsitem.title: USA: Judge gives KIWI week to get new financial plan.
newsitem.headline: Judge gives KIWI week to get new financial plan.

text.p: Federal bankruptcy judge on Friday gave Kiwi International Airlines one week to put its financing backing in order.

Federal Judge Rosemary Gambardella ruled that the Newark-based airline can continue to expend funds for skeleton operations for another week while it tries to repair a debtor-in-possession plan that apparently has fallen through.
The ruling came after Gambardella learned that a financial plan backed the Wasatch International Group of Boynton, Florida was hitting snags.

The judge was told that Wasatch may not make to Kiwi the previously agreed upon 10 weekly payments of $500,000 that were to being this week and that the first payment made was only $100,000. The judge told Kiwi lawyer Howard Greenberg to return next Friday with either completed payments from Wasatch or a new financial backer.

Opposing this plan was Summit Bancorp, the airline's secured creditor, which said it threatened the protections for its $1.1 million loan. The judge ruled that the protections are adequate for one more week.
Kiwi sought protection under bankruptcy laws on September 30 and three weeks later suspended remaining flight service.
